change_kind: feature

# Crew Chatter: accounts and core notes

This is feature 1 of 7 split from docs/features/crew-chatter/design.md. It builds on nothing and lays the foundation that the other six features extend. It uses the repository's existing npm-workspace scaffold: an Express 5 + TypeScript backend in `backend/` and a React 19 + Vite + TypeScript frontend in `frontend/`. It delivers:

- email/password registration, sign-in, and password reset
- persisted notes with creation and last-updated timestamps
- a rich-text editor that auto-saves
- checklist items with progress and an "Open tasks" filter
- the desktop and mobile layouts

## Scope

- Accounts: register, sign in, and reset a forgotten password with an email address and password. The password is persisted only as a hash.
- Persistence: user and note records, managed through `backend/src/db.ts`. Each note record includes its creation and last-updated timestamps and its checklist data.
- Notes API: create, read, list, and update the signed-in user's own notes through `backend/src/routes/notes.ts`. An error handler in `backend/src/app.ts` turns unexpected handler failures into HTTP 500 JSON responses that reveal no implementation details.
- Dashboard: the signed-in user's note list, a "New note" button, an empty state for a user with no notes, and an "Open tasks" filter.
- Editor:
  - title and body fields
  - formatting controls for heading, bold, italic, bulleted list, numbered list, checklist, link, block quote, and code block
  - plain-text and HTML paste
  - Unicode content
  - checklist items whose checkboxes toggle in the editor, with "N of M complete" progress
- Auto-save: there is no Save button. Edits save after typing stops, through `frontend/src/hooks/useAutoSave.ts`. A save-state indicator shows "Saving", "Saved", "Unable to save", or "Offline". A pending or in-flight save is protected when the user closes or reloads the tab and when they navigate within the app.
- Layout: at desktop width, the left navigation sidebar, note list, and editor panel sit side by side. At mobile width, the sidebar becomes a drawer opened by a menu button, and the editor spans the viewport width. The user can move through the note list and open notes with the keyboard alone.

## Out of scope

- Every criterion the split assigns to another feature, as listed in this feature's design:
  - crew-chatter-hardening: sign-out and its HTTP 401 behavior, cross-user isolation checks, persistence across a backend restart, confirmation labels, accessibility checks, and actionable error wording
  - crew-chatter-search: the "Untitled note" label, search, and mobile browser support
  - crew-chatter-note-lifecycle: activity records, dashboard sections, sorting, filters, pinning, archive, and trash
  - crew-chatter-folders-tags: note-row details, folders, and tags
  - crew-chatter-attachments-versions: attachments and version history
  - crew-chatter-export-import: export and import
- Google or other OAuth sign-in, which the design describes as a future enhancement.
- Visual tone guidance: a calm, focused, lightweight feel, generous line height, and restrained formatting controls. This guidance has no pass/fail check and is not a criterion.

## Verification notes

The delivered code must pass the repository's own scripts, as defined in the root `package.json`, the workspace `package.json` files, and `governed.yaml`.

- `npm ci` installs exactly from the root `package-lock.json`, which covers both workspaces. Any dependency added to `backend/package.json` or `frontend/package.json` must also be recorded in `package-lock.json`.
- `npm run typecheck` runs `tsc --noEmit` in each workspace with strict mode, using the existing `backend/tsconfig.json` and `frontend/tsconfig.json`. The frontend config also includes `frontend/vite.config.ts`. The backend config uses `module: NodeNext`, so relative imports between backend source files use explicit `.js` extensions. Backend source stays under `backend/src`, and frontend source stays under `frontend/src`.
- `npm run lint` runs `eslint .` with the existing `eslint.config.js`, which applies the React Hooks rules to frontend files.
- `npm run build` runs `tsc` in `backend/` and `vite build` in `frontend/`. Both write to `dist/` directories, which `.gitignore` already ignores.
- If the backend creates a local database file at runtime, `.gitignore` must cover its path.

## Declared artifacts

backend/src/app.ts
backend/src/auth.ts
backend/src/config.ts
backend/src/db.ts
backend/src/index.ts
backend/src/routes/notes.ts
frontend/package.json

frontend/src/api.ts
frontend/src/components/AuthScreen.tsx

frontend/src/components/NoteList.tsx

frontend/src/styles.css
package-lock.json

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-001: Registering with an email address not yet in use and a non-empty password creates an account, signs the user in, and displays that user's notes dashboard.
- AC-002: Registering with an email address that is already registered is rejected with an error message and no second account is created.
- AC-003: Signing in with a registered email and its correct password displays that user's dashboard, and signing in with an incorrect password displays an error message and leaves the user signed out.
- AC-005: After a password reset is requested for a registered email and completed with a new password, signing in with the new password succeeds and signing in with the old password fails.
- AC-006: The persisted user record stores the password only as a hash in its password hash field, and no persisted field contains the submitted plaintext password.
- AC-010: Clicking the "New note" button on the dashboard creates a note and opens it in the editor with keyboard focus in the title or body field.
- AC-011: The editor provides controls for heading, bold, italic, bulleted list, numbered list, checklist, link, block quote, and code block, and content formatted with each control keeps that formatting after the page is reloaded.
- AC-012: The editor has no Save button, and an edit to the title or body is persisted with no manual save action once typing stops, so that after the indicator shows "Saved" a page reload shows the edit.
- AC-013: The save-state indicator shows "Saving" while a save request is in flight, "Saved" after it succeeds, "Unable to save" after a save fails while the browser is online, and "Offline" while navigator.onLine is false.
- AC-014: A note whose title and body both contain the text "Crew 日本語 émoji 🎉 العربية" displays that exact text in both fields after it is saved and the page is reloaded.
- AC-015: Pasting text/plain or text/html clipboard content into the note body inserts the pasted text into the body and the note saves it.
- AC-016: Closing or reloading the tab while a save is pending or in flight triggers the browser's leave-page confirmation, and closing or reloading the tab with no pending save does not.
- AC-018: Every note records a creation timestamp and a last-updated timestamp, and saving an edit changes the last-updated timestamp while leaving the creation timestamp unchanged.
- AC-023: When the signed-in user has no notes, the dashboard displays an empty-state message and a button that creates the user's first note when clicked.
- AC-049: The editor can insert a checklist item into a note, and toggling an item's checkbox in the editor marks it complete or incomplete, and that state persists after the page is reloaded.
- AC-050: The "Open tasks" filter lists every note with at least one incomplete checklist item and excludes notes whose checklist items are all complete and notes with no checklist items.
- AC-051: A note with checklist items displays progress in the form "N of M complete", where M is its number of checklist items and N is the number marked complete.
- AC-064: At a 1280×800 viewport the app shows the left navigation sidebar, the note list, and the editor panel side by side.
- AC-065: At a 375×667 viewport the navigation sidebar is hidden behind a menu button that opens it as a drawer, and an opened note's editor spans the full viewport width.
- AC-066: Using only the keyboard, the user can move through every note in the note list and open any of them in the editor.
- AC-069: When a backend request handler fails unexpectedly, the API responds with HTTP 500 and a JSON body whose message contains no stack trace, file path, or database query text.
- AC-070: With the backend running on the same machine as the browser, the editor appears within 200 ms of clicking "New note".
- AC-072: While a save is pending or in flight, navigating within the app to another note or view either completes the save before the switch takes effect or asks the user to confirm leaving, so the pending edit is never silently lost.
- AC-077: With the backend running on the same machine as the browser, typed text appears in the note editor within 200 ms of each keystroke.

## Open decisions

- OD-001 (high): How does a user who has requested a password reset get the reset token or link needed to finish the reset, given that the design names no email delivery mechanism (for example, an email sent through a named provider, a token written to the backend log, or a token shown in the UI)?
- OD-002 (medium): What debounce interval does auto-save wait after typing stops before saving, given that the design gives 500–1,000 milliseconds only as an example?

# Plan: Crew Chatter accounts and core notes

## Approach

- No new dependencies. The backend uses Express 5 and Node built-ins: `node:sqlite` (`DatabaseSync`, typed by the existing `@types/node` 24 and available without a flag from Node 22.13) for storage, and `node:crypto` (`scrypt`, `randomBytes`, `randomUUID`, `timingSafeEqual`, `createHash`) for IDs, password hashes and tokens. The frontend uses React 19, a `contentEditable` editor driven by `document.execCommand`, and a sanitizer built on DOMParser. So `backend/package.json`, `frontend/package.json` and `package-lock.json` stay unchanged. If a dependency is ever added, the same change must record it in `package-lock.json`.
- Sessions: a random token in an httpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored, in a `sessions` table. The frontend calls `/api` on the same origin (the existing Vite proxy to port 3000 in development).
- OD-001 (provisional, needs product confirmation): a reset request always gets the same generic reply. For a registered email, the backend also creates a single-use token that expires after 30 minutes and is stored hashed, and writes the link `<APP_URL>/?reset=<token>` to the backend log. The token is never returned in an HTTP response or shown in the UI. Delivery lives in one function in `backend/src/auth.ts`, so an email provider can replace it later.
- OD-002 (provisional): auto-save waits 750 ms after typing stops. The value is a single named constant in `frontend/src/hooks/useAutoSave.ts`.
- Checklist markup: a `ul` with `data-checklist` set to `true`, whose `li` items carry `data-checked` set to `true` or `false`. Everywhere in this plan, a checklist item is an `li` element that carries a `data-checked` attribute; the backend counter and the editor progress text both use this definition. On every write, the backend recomputes the counts from the stored body and saves them on the note row, so the Open tasks filter and the list progress never rely on counts sent by the client.
- The backend stores the note body as an opaque string and never renders it. The frontend sanitizes body HTML with an allowlist before it enters the editor, both when a stored note is loaded and when HTML is pasted.
- Express 5 leaves `req.body` undefined when no JSON body was parsed, so every handler that reads a body first checks that it is an object and returns 400 with a generic message if it is not.
- Relative backend imports use `.js` extensions (NodeNext). The default database file is `backend/data/crew-chatter.db`, resolved as `../data/crew-chatter.db` relative to `import.meta.url`. This gives the same path whether the code runs from `backend/src` or from `backend/dist`, and `.gitignore` covers it.
- In-app navigation uses only `history.replaceState`, so it creates no in-app history entries and every in-app switch passes through the navigation guard in `frontend/src/App.tsx`.

## Tasks

- Update `.gitignore` to ignore `backend/data/` and SQLite files (`*.db`, `*.db-journal`, `*.db-wal`, `*.db-shm`) so the runtime database is never tracked.
- Create `backend/src/config.ts` exporting a frozen config read from environment variables, with these defaults: port (PORT, 3000), database path (DATABASE_PATH, default `../data/crew-chatter.db` resolved from `import.meta.url` with `fileURLToPath`), app URL (APP_URL, default `http://localhost:5173`), secure cookies (true when NODE_ENV is production), session lifetime (30 days), reset token lifetime (30 minutes) and JSON body limit (5 MB, enough for a 1,000,000-character body of multi-byte text after JSON escaping).
- Create `backend/src/db.ts` exporting `initDb()`. It creates the database directory, opens a `DatabaseSync` at the configured path, turns on foreign keys and WAL mode, and creates these tables if they do not exist: `users` (id text primary key from `randomUUID`; email UNIQUE, stored trimmed and lower-cased; password_hash; created_at), `sessions` (token_hash primary key, user_id foreign key, expires_at), `password_resets` (token_hash primary key, user_id foreign key, expires_at, used_at) and `notes` (id text primary key from `randomUUID`, user_id foreign key, title, body, checklist_total, checklist_done, created_at, updated_at). Add an index on notes (user_id, updated_at).
- In `backend/src/db.ts`, export typed data-access functions that use the handle opened by `initDb()` and only prepared statements with bound parameters. Users: create, find by email, find by id, update password hash. User creation catches only the unique-constraint violation (node:sqlite errcode 2067, SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE), returns null for it, and rethrows any other error. Sessions: create, find valid, delete all for a user. Reset tokens: create, consume. Notes: create, get by id and owner, list by owner (with an optional open-tasks flag meaning checklist_done < checklist_total), update by id and owner. Return camelCase objects, and read password_hash only in the auth lookups.
- In `backend/src/db.ts`, give a new note the same UTC ISO-8601 value for created_at and updated_at. On update, write only updated_at: use the current time, or one millisecond after the previous value if the clock has not moved on. Never change created_at.
- Create `backend/src/auth.ts` with scrypt password hashing (promisified): a random 16-byte salt, with the parameters and salt stored alongside the hash in password_hash. Verify with `timingSafeEqual`. Never store, log or return the plaintext password.
- In `backend/src/auth.ts`, add session helpers. Create a random 32-byte token and store its SHA-256 hash. Set it in an httpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie with path `/`, marked Secure when configured. Parse the Cookie header by hand. Add a `requireAuth` middleware that stores the user id in `res.locals` or returns a 401 JSON response.
- In `backend/src/auth.ts`, export an auth router with three routes. Each route that reads a body first checks that `req.body` is an object. POST `/register`: validate the email format and require a non-empty password. If user creation returns null because the email is already in use, return 409 with the message An account with this email already exists., so no second row is ever written. Otherwise start a session and return 201 with the user. POST `/login`: for an unknown email, first verify the submitted password against a fixed dummy scrypt hash so the response time matches a wrong password, then return 401 with the message Incorrect email or password. and create no session; for a wrong password, return 401 with the same message and create no session; otherwise start a session and return 200 with the user. GET `/me`: return the current user, or 401.
- In `backend/src/auth.ts`, add POST `/reset-request` and POST `/reset-complete`. `/reset-request` always returns 200 with a generic message. For a registered email it also creates a hashed single-use token and passes the link to a `deliverResetLink` function, which writes it to the log. `/reset-complete` checks that the token is unexpired and unused and that the new password is not empty. It then replaces the password hash, marks the token used and deletes the user's existing sessions. It returns 400 with a clear message for an invalid or expired token.
- Create `backend/src/routes/notes.ts` exporting a router behind `requireAuth`. GET `/` returns summaries (id, title, checklistTotal, checklistDone, createdAt, updatedAt), newest updatedAt first. With the query `filter=open-tasks`, it returns only notes with at least one incomplete checklist item. POST `/` creates an empty note and returns 201 with the full note. GET `/:id` and PATCH `/:id` are limited to the owner and return 404 JSON when the note is not found.
- In `backend/src/routes/notes.ts`, validate PATCH input. The body must be an object; `title` and `body` are optional strings; title may be up to 500 characters and body up to 1,000,000 characters; anything else gets a 400. Before saving, recompute checklist_total as the number of `li` start tags that carry a `data-checked` attribute in the body, and checklist_done as the number of those whose value is true, using one linear-time scan that finds each `<li` start tag with `indexOf` and reads the tag up to its next `>`, with no backtracking regular expression over the body, so unclosed tags cannot stall the event loop. Return the full updated note, including checklistTotal, checklistDone, createdAt and updatedAt.
- Create `backend/src/app.ts` exporting `createApp()`. Mount a JSON parser with the configured limit, `/api/health`, the `/api/auth` router and the `/api/notes` router. Return a JSON 404 for unmatched `/api` routes. Add a final four-argument error handler, typed without `any`. If headers are already sent, it passes the error on with `next(err)`. An error from the JSON parser that carries a 4xx status (malformed JSON 400, body too large 413, unsupported charset 415) gets that status and a generic message. Any other error is logged on the server and gets a 500 with a JSON body whose `error` field reads Something went wrong. Please try again. No response ever includes a stack trace, file path or SQL text.
- Rewrite `backend/src/index.ts` to call `initDb()` from `db.ts`, build the app with `createApp()` from `app.ts`, and listen on the configured port.
- Create `frontend/src/api.ts` with a typed fetch wrapper (same-origin credentials, JSON bodies). It throws `ApiError` (holding the status and the server's `error` message) when the server returns an error, and `NetworkError` when the request never reaches the server. Export the `User`, `NoteSummary` and `Note` types and the functions `getMe`, `register`, `login`, `requestPasswordReset`, `completePasswordReset`, `listNotes`, `createNote`, `getNote` and `updateNote`.
- Create `frontend/src/components/AuthScreen.tsx` with four modes: sign in, register, forgot password and set new password. Use labelled email and password inputs and show API error messages inline. Show a confirmation message after a reset request. Open the set-new-password mode when the URL has a `reset` query parameter. When the reset succeeds, remove that parameter with `history.replaceState` and switch to sign-in mode with a message that the password was updated. Call `onAuthenticated(user)` after a successful registration or sign-in.
- Create `frontend/src/hooks/useAutoSave.ts`. It takes the note id, the current title and body, a save function that resolves to the saved note, and an `onSaved(note)` callback. It saves 750 ms after the last change and runs one save at a time, so the latest edit is always written last. It tracks `navigator.onLine` with online and offline listeners. The `status` it returns is one of idle, saving, saved, error or offline, with the display labels Saving, Saved, Unable to save and Offline. The status is saving while a change waits for the debounce or a request is in flight. It is saved only after a successful response when the saved title and body equal the latest values. It is error after a failed save while the browser is online, and offline whenever navigator.onLine is false. The hook also returns `hasPendingChanges` and an async `flush()` that saves at once and resolves to whether every edit is stored.
- In `frontend/src/hooks/useAutoSave.ts`, add a `beforeunload` listener that calls `preventDefault()` and sets `returnValue` only while a save is pending or in flight. Retry a pending save when the browser comes back online. Keep mutable values in refs so the dependency arrays stay complete under the React Hooks lint rules. On unmount, clear the timer, remove the listeners, and ignore state updates from a request that finishes after unmount.
- Create `frontend/src/components/NoteEditor.tsx`, keyed by note id. It has a labelled title input with `maxLength` 500 and a toolbar for heading, bold, italic, bulleted list, numbered list, checklist, link, block quote and code block. On mount it calls `execCommand` with `styleWithCSS` set to false and `defaultParagraphSeparator` set to p, so formatting produces tags rather than styled spans. Bold and italic use the `bold` and `italic` commands. Heading, block quote and code block use `formatBlock` with `<h2>`, `<blockquote>` and `<pre>`. The lists use `insertUnorderedList` and `insertOrderedList`. Link uses `createLink` with a URL from `window.prompt`, accepted only when it is http, https or mailto. The toolbar buttons call `preventDefault` on mouse down to keep the editor selection. The body is an uncontrolled `contentEditable` element, loaded once per note, and its HTML is read from the DOM on input, so typing never re-renders the body.
- In `frontend/src/components/NoteEditor.tsx`, add an allowlist sanitizer built on DOMParser. Allowed elements: p, div, br, h1 to h3, strong, b, em, i, ul, ol, li, blockquote, pre, code and a. Allowed attributes: `href` on links (http, https or mailto only), `data-checklist` on ul, and `data-checked` (true or false) on li. Remove script, style, iframe, object and similar elements together with their content, and unwrap any other element so only its text remains. Run the sanitizer on stored body HTML before loading it and on pasted HTML.
- In `frontend/src/components/NoteEditor.tsx`, handle paste: prevent the default, insert sanitized text/html with `insertHTML` or text/plain with `insertText`, then tell auto-save about the change.
- In `frontend/src/components/NoteEditor.tsx`, implement the checklist control so it inserts a checklist list with one unchecked item. A click on an item counts as a toggle when its horizontal offset from the item's left edge falls inside the item's left padding, where the checkbox is drawn. Pressing Ctrl+Enter inside the item also toggles it. A toggle flips `data-checked` and then tells auto-save. After an `insertParagraph` input inside a checklist item, set the item now holding the caret to `data-checked` false. On each input, give any li inside a `data-checklist` list that lacks `data-checked` the value false. Whenever the note has at least one checklist item, show N of M complete, computed from the editor DOM by counting li elements with `data-checked` (M) and those with the value true (N).
- In `frontend/src/components/NoteEditor.tsx`, show the save-state label from `useAutoSave` in an `aria-live` polite region. Pass the parent's `onSaved` callback through to the hook. Focus the title input on mount when the note was just created. Give the parent a navigation guard callback built on the hook's `flush` and pending state. Render a back button for the mobile layout.
- Create `frontend/src/components/NoteList.tsx`. Show the notes as a list of buttons, each with the title, the last-updated time and, when the note has checklist items, N of M complete. A row with an empty title shows only its time and gets an accessible name based on that time; the Untitled note label belongs to crew-chatter-search. Use a roving tabindex so Tab reaches the list, Up and Down arrows move between rows, and Enter or Space opens the focused note. When the list is empty, the all-notes view shows No notes yet with a Create your first note button, and the open-tasks view shows No open tasks.
- Create `frontend/src/components/Sidebar.tsx`: a `nav` element with the New note button and the All notes and Open tasks view buttons, with `aria-current` on the active view. Give it an id that the menu button references through `aria-controls`. When it is open as the mobile drawer, close it on Escape, on a backdrop click or after a selection.
- Rewrite `frontend/src/App.tsx`, keeping the named export `App` that `main.tsx` imports. On start, load the session with `getMe`, and show `AuthScreen` when signed out. Its `onAuthenticated` callback stores the user and shows the dashboard in the all-notes view. When signed in, render a header with the mobile menu button (with `aria-expanded`), then `Sidebar`, `NoteList` and the editor panel. The editor panel holds `NoteEditor` for the selected note, or a placeholder message when no note is selected, so the desktop layout always shows three panes. Keep the selected note id and the current view in state, and mirror the note id to the `note` query parameter with `history.replaceState` so a reload reopens the same note.
- In `frontend/src/App.tsx`, send every in-app switch (opening another note, changing view, creating a note, mobile back) through a navigation guard. The guard waits for the editor's `flush()`; if the save failed or the browser is offline, it asks with `window.confirm` before switching. For New note, call `createNote`, add the result at the top of the list, and open it straight away with focus in the title. The view must not wait on anything other than that one create request.
- In `frontend/src/App.tsx`, use each successful save response to update the note's list summary (title, checklist counts, updatedAt) and move it to the top, so the list shows saved edits without refetching on every keystroke. In the open-tasks view, remove the summary when checklistDone is not less than checklistTotal, and keep or add it while an incomplete item remains. Refetch the list when the view changes.
- Update `frontend/src/main.tsx` to import `./styles.css`.
- Create `frontend/src/styles.css`. Use system fonts with generous line height. From 768px wide, lay the app out as a full-height three-column grid with the menu button hidden: the sidebar about 220px, the note list about 300px, and the editor panel taking the rest. Below 768px, make the sidebar a fixed off-canvas drawer with a backdrop, opened by the visible menu button. The note list fills the screen until a note is opened; the open editor panel then spans 100% of the viewport width and the list is hidden.
- In `frontend/src/styles.css`, style the editor toolbar, the save-state indicator, the empty state, the editor placeholder, and visible focus outlines on list rows and controls. Checklist items have no bullets, a checkbox drawn with `::before` in the item's left padding, and a checked state that is marked and struck through.

# Plan: Crew Chatter accounts and core notes

## Approach

- No new dependencies. The backend uses Express 5 and Node built-ins: `node:sqlite` (`DatabaseSync`) for storage, and `node:crypto` (`scrypt`, `randomBytes`, `timingSafeEqual`, `createHash`) for password hashes and tokens. The frontend uses React 19, a `contentEditable` editor driven by `document.execCommand`, and a sanitizer built on DOMParser. So `backend/package.json`, `frontend/package.json` and `package-lock.json` stay unchanged. If a dependency is ever added, the same change must record it in `package-lock.json`.
- Sessions: a random token in an httpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored, in a `sessions` table. The frontend calls `/api` on the same origin (the existing Vite proxy in development).
- OD-001 (provisional, needs product confirmation): a reset request always gets the same generic reply. For a registered email, the backend also creates a single-use token that expires after 30 minutes and is stored hashed, and writes the link `<APP_URL>/?reset=<token>` to the backend log. The token is never returned in an HTTP response or shown in the UI. Delivery lives in one function in `backend/src/auth.ts`, so an email provider can replace it later.
- OD-002 (provisional): auto-save waits 750 ms after typing stops. The value is a single named constant in `frontend/src/hooks/useAutoSave.ts`.
- Checklist markup: a `ul` with `data-checklist` set to true, whose `li` items have `data-checked` set to true or false. On every write, the backend counts checklist items from the stored body and saves the counts on the note row. The Open tasks filter and the progress text therefore never rely on counts sent by the client.
- Relative backend imports use `.js` extensions (NodeNext). By default the database file is `backend/data/crew-chatter.db`, which `.gitignore` covers.

## Tasks

- Update `.gitignore` to ignore `backend/data/` and SQLite files (`*.db`, `*.db-journal`, `*.db-wal`, `*.db-shm`) so the runtime database is never tracked.

- Create `backend/src/db.ts`. Open a `DatabaseSync` at the configured path, creating its directory first. Turn on foreign keys and WAL mode. Create these tables if they do not exist: `users` (id primary key; email UNIQUE, stored trimmed and lower-cased; password_hash; created_at), `sessions` (token_hash primary key, user_id foreign key, expires_at), `password_resets` (token_hash primary key, user_id foreign key, expires_at, used_at) and `notes` (id, user_id foreign key, title, body, checklist_total, checklist_done, created_at, updated_at). Add an index on notes (user_id, updated_at).
- In `backend/src/db.ts`, export typed data-access functions that use only prepared statements with bound parameters. Users: create, find by email, find by id, update password hash. Sessions: create, find valid, delete all for a user. Reset tokens: create, consume. Notes: create, get by id and owner, list by owner (with an optional open-tasks flag meaning checklist_done < checklist_total), update by id and owner. Return camelCase objects, and read password_hash only in the auth lookups.
- In `backend/src/db.ts`, give a new note the same UTC ISO-8601 value for created_at and updated_at. On update, write only updated_at: use the current time, or one millisecond after the previous value if the clock has not moved on. Never change created_at.
- Create `backend/src/auth.ts` with scrypt password hashing: a random 16-byte salt, with the parameters and salt stored alongside the hash in password_hash. Verify with `timingSafeEqual`. Never store, log or return the plaintext password.
- In `backend/src/auth.ts`, add session helpers. Create a random 32-byte token and store its SHA-256 hash. Set it in an httpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie with path `/`, marked Secure when configured. Parse the Cookie header by hand. Add a `requireAuth` middleware that stores the user id in `res.locals` or returns a 401 JSON response.
- In `backend/src/auth.ts`, export an auth router with three routes. POST `/register`: validate the email format and require a non-empty password. For an email already in use, return 409 with the message An account with this email already exists., relying on the UNIQUE constraint so no second row is ever written. Otherwise create the user, start a session and return 201 with the user. POST `/login`: for an unknown email or a wrong password, return 401 with the message Incorrect email or password. and create no session. GET `/me`: return the current user, or 401.
- In `backend/src/auth.ts`, add POST `/reset-request` and POST `/reset-complete`. `/reset-request` always returns 200 with a generic message. For a registered email it also creates a hashed single-use token and passes the link to a `deliverResetLink` function, which writes it to the log. `/reset-complete` checks that the token is unexpired and unused and that the new password is not empty. It then replaces the password hash, marks the token used and deletes the user's existing sessions. It returns 400 with a clear message for an invalid or expired token.

With the query `filter=open-tasks`, it returns only notes with at least one incomplete checklist item. POST `/` creates an empty note and returns 201 with the full note. GET `/:id` and PATCH `/:id` are limited to the owner and return 404 JSON when the note is not found.
